bug_info.bug_desc: In CPHA=1 mode the FSM intentionally delays byte_starting, byte_ending, and bit_shifting pulses by one state transition using the *_cpha0_q registers. However the non-delayed command-side signals used with those delayed pulses were not delayed: speed_o was tied to cmd_speed_q, rd_en_internal was gated by cmd_rd_en_q, cmd_len was not latched, and the single shared byte_cntr was loaded/decremented on new_command/byte_ending regardless of CPHA. In back-to-back or keep-active operation a new segment can be accepted at the same boundary where the previous CPHA=1 segment still has delayed transfer pulses, so those delayed pulses are evaluated with the next segment's speed, read-enable, length, or byte count. This can suppress or misattribute the final receive-byte request, corrupt the byte counter, and produce incorrect last_read/last_write or SD output-enable timing on the last bit.
bug_info.fix_hint: Maintain explicit delayed copies of the CPHA=1-side control values (speed_cpha1, segment_rd_en_cpha1, new_command_cpha1) and latch the command length into cmd_len_q. Use separate byte counters for CPHA=0 and CPHA=1 so the delayed CPHA=1 byte_ending decrements the previous segment count before the next command is loaded. Drive speed_o, sd_en_o, rd_en_internal, and last_read/last_write from the appropriate delayed or early copies, using byte_cntr_early/late for the last-byte markers.
